transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-21
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Nina (Redwood SE), Marcus (CSM), Sofia (AtlasPay VP Eng), Daniel (AtlasPay SRE), Priya (AtlasPay Head PM)

Summary:
Quick follow-up on yesterday's production backpressure incident. Goal: hand off mitigations and agree next steps for benching, runbook adoption, and alerting changes. Discussed short-term throttles, adaptive batching, circuit-breaker thresholds, and audit log / KMS considerations for enterprise compliance.

Topics covered:
- Incident recap and primary hypothesis (KV cache storm + bursty traffic from nightly job)
- Immediate mitigations (prefix caching, route-level throttles, surge autoscale tuning)
- Long-term: canary rollout, priority queuing, dedicated capacity evaluation
- Security/observability: audit logs, KMS rotation, SOC2 questions for private deployment

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan: ok uh folks thanks for joining on short notice, i know you all had a rough morning so i'll let sofia start with a quick recap from atlas pay side if that's okay
[00:18] Sofia: yeah thanks jordan, uh so between 03:30 and 04:10 utc we saw sustained 10x request spikes to the /generate endpoint, latency climbed and then token errors spiked, the app fell back to a lower fidelity model and some payments workflows slowed, it looked like a KV cache miss storm triggered regen for large contexts
[00:41] Daniel: to add, our telemetry shows a sudden increase in seq len and concurrent kv lookups, could be the nightly reconciliation job that hits multiple accounts in parallel, we had partial throttles but the circuit didn't trip fast enough
[01:05] Nina: got it, thanks for that. from our side hypothesis is similar — prefix/K V cache pressure combined with continuous batching clumps caused head-of-line blocking. we also noticed model fallback increased token count which amplified load, so there's a feedback loop
[01:33] Priya: quick Q — was there anything in the rollout yesterday? we did push a small prompt-change earlier but not a model change
[01:42] Jordan: no model change on our side, looks like workload pattern change. thanks for clarifying priya
[01:50] Sofia: lisa (not on call) ran a quick spike test and said it matched morning traffic shape so we think it's data driven from reconciliation
[02:10] Nina: ok, so short term mitigation checklist we recommend: 1) emergency route-level throttles, 2) decrease continuous-batch window for that tenant route, 3) enable prefix cache warmers for heavy accounts, 4) add a circuit breaker threshold to quickly failover to a cheap fallback path rather than piling up requests
[02:38] Daniel: about throttles — we worry about user-visible errors for payments flows. we'd prefer graceful queueing not hard 429s. can we do soft throttling or queued backpressure?
[02:56] Jordan: yes, we support configurable backpressure where Redwood returns a 202 queued token and a retry-after header, or we can route to a lower-tier model automatically. tradeoff: queued work increases latency, routing to smaller model increases potential quality regressions
[03:18] Nina: also worth mentioning adaptive batching: if we detect burst on single tenant id we switch to per-tenant batching limit and cap batch sizes. that reduces head-of-line blocking without global perf hit
[03:40] Sofia: that sounds good. how invasive is prefix warming? can your team run an initial warm pass for top 200 accounts?
[03:51] Marcus: we can run a one-off warm and hand you a script to run periodically. will need list of keys and a dev account to avoid prod token misuse
[04:08] Daniel: we'll provide scrubbed keys and tokenized traces; security is a thing — we need KMS-backed key rotation and proof of how runbook is executed inside our VPC
[04:25] Jordan: understood. for private/dedicated setups we support KMS integration (HSM optional). nina, can you highlight what artifacts we'll share?
[04:36] Nina: sure — we'll share a runbook (link: https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/backpressure-atlaspay) that includes playbook steps, config diffs, and a minimal script to warm prefix cache. also a benchmark harness and sample traces template. note: link is placeholder — we'll send final via shared doc
[04:58] Priya: perfect. on compliance — we need audit logs that show each mitigation action and admin who triggered it, is that available in hosted offering?
[05:09] Marcus: yes, audit logs for redwood console include action, timestamp, actor; retention tiers vary by plan. for enterprise/private we can extend retention and push to your SIEM via secure forwarder
[05:32] Daniel: SOC 2 scope question — is the mitigation action path within scope or is that customer-side? we need evidence for our regulator
[05:43] Jordan: both. our audit trail will show Redwood-side actions; your triggers and account-level changes should be in your incident doc. we'll provide a compliance packet and sign off statements as needed
[05:58] Sofia: ok great. can we talk tradeoffs: dedicated capacity vs tuned hosted lanes? what would you recommend for atlaspay given traffic pattern?
[06:10] Nina: if bursts are infrequent and cost sensitivity high, we recommend hosted with aggressive backpressure and adaptive batching. if bursts are frequent and SLA critical, Dedicated pools with reserved capacity and pre-warming reduce risk, but cost is higher. there is also a hybrid route: reserved baseline + on-demand burstable lanes
[06:34] Daniel: hybrid sounds attractive. do you support region affinity and cross-region fallback? we have EU + US compliance needs
[06:44] Jordan: yes, smart routing supports region affinity + failover. we can pin tenant to EU primary and US fallback, and encrypt egress with customer-managed KMS in VPC/private deployments
[07:01] Sofia: next, we want concrete thresholds for the circuit breaker. what metric do you suggest? p99 latency? queue depth? kv cache miss rate?
[07:12] Nina: good Q. best practice: combine simple signals — sustained p95 or p99 latency above threshold for X minutes and queue depth > Y and kv-miss-rate spike. for example: p95 > 1.2s for 2 minutes AND queue-depth > 100 triggers soft circuit, then p99 > 2s for 30s triggers hard cutover to fallback model
[07:42] Priya: can we have those presets in the runbook so we can tune them? the product team prefers starting defaults
[07:49] Jordan: yes we'll include recommended presets and guidance on tuning per tenant.
[07:55] Daniel: we will need a smoke test plan to validate an emergency throttle won't break the payments flow entirely
[08:03] Marcus: we'll provide a smoke checklist and test harness that simulates 2x and 10x bursts with synthetic payloads
[08:12] Sofia: okay thanks. let's move to observability — what new dashboards should we add?
[08:19] Nina: add per-route token cost, p50/p95/p99 latency, queue depth, kv-miss rate, batch size distribution, and model-fallback ratio. we also recommend a synthetic probe hitting critical payment path every 30s
[08:37] Daniel: do you have sample grafana dashboards or can we pull via API?
[08:42] Marcus: yes public dashboards exist, and you can pull metrics via our metrics API; we'll share dashboard json exports
[08:51] Priya: what about tracing? we use jaeger — can we get end-to-end traces including redwood spans?
[08:58] Nina: we export opentelemetry spans; with private deployment we can push spans to your jaeger/tempo, with hosted we provide trace links in console and can push sampled spans to your endpoint under contract
[09:14] Sofia: good. let's discuss timeline and ownership — we want mitigation on by EOD friday and benching next week
[09:24] Jordan: feasible. proposed timeline: today-runbook sent; by EOD friday one soft throttle rule + prefix warming; next week we'll run bench and adjust circuit thresholds; follow-up checkin 2026-06-01
[09:40] Daniel: any risk of data residency being violated during prefix warming? we need to ensure no PII leaves our control
[09:48] Nina: the prefix warmer only touches model input context and uses tokenized keys; we will accept a scrubbed trace and use your dev VPC credentials — no PII should be transmitted to Redwood hosted without customer consent. for private deployments we can perform warming entirely in your VPC
[10:07] Sofia: noted. can you put that in writing in the runbook? we need legal signoff
[10:12] Jordan: yes, we'll add a security appendix that details data handling, KMS usage, and scrub process
[10:20] Priya: question about cost: if we add prefix warming and reserved baseline will cost jump significantly? need rough order magnitude
[10:27] Marcus: rough: warming run is one-time small compute; reserved baseline depends on committed GPUs — we can model current spend vs reserved vs hybrid in a short spreadsheet and share. anticipate 10-30% uplift for reserved baseline depending on burst headroom required
[10:44] Daniel: ok send the cost model, we'll review with finance
[10:48] Jordan: will do.
[10:52] Sofia: any blockers from redwood side for EOD friday mitigation?
[10:56] Nina: need scrubbed traces and dev VPC creds, and agreement on throttle rule (we'll propose default). once we have that we can push soft throttle via console in under 2 hours for hosted lane
[11:10] Sofia: we'll try to deliver traces by Sunday 05:00 UTC if possible
[11:16] Daniel: yes we'll prioritize it
[11:19] Jordan: great.
[11:22] -- mid-call technical deep-dive --
[11:30] Nina: diving into the internals briefly: redwood uses continuous batching and kv cache to reduce per-token compute. when kv cache misses occur at scale, the runtime does additional attention recompute which adds latency; if too many misses align in same window you get head-of-line and the batching window grows, harming latency. optimizations: per-tenant batch caps, prefix caching, smaller micro-batch windows, and priority queues for critical endpoints
[12:05] Daniel: are any of these changes risky for long tail request correctness? we worry about reordering in priority queue
[12:14] Nina: priority queue maintains order per request id for payments flows; only non-critical lower-priority requests can be re-ordered or delayed. we will not reorder requests within same payment transaction id
[12:33] Sofia: can you do a dry-run of queue changes in staging?
[12:37] Nina: yes, that's part of the bench plan
[12:40] -- around 30 min mark we discussed metrics and bench details --
[30:05] Marcus: recap of bench plan: 1) provide scrubbed traces, 2) we run 1:1 dev VPC bench (no PII), 3) measure p50/p95/p99 and queue depth at 1x, 4x, 10x burst patterns, 4) recommend config diffs
[30:26] Daniel: what about load generation — can you reproduce kv-miss pattern? our reco job is multi-account traversal which is heavy on context size
[30:34] Nina: yes we can parameterize trace replayers to simulate multi-account traversal and inject variable seq lengths
[30:42] Priya: we'll also want to measure user-perceived latency for checkout flow — can you instrument synthetic transaction latency?
[30:50] Marcus: yes synthetic probes and traced checkout path will be included in the report
[30:58] Sofia: great. regulatory note: we might need an exec summary for legal and a CSV of audit events once mitigations roll out
[31:08] Jordan: we'll provide an exec summary template and exportable audit csv for each mitigation action
[31:18] -- final 15 minutes: decisions and explicit next steps --
[33:02] Jordan: ok decisions so far: 1) enable soft throttling + prefix warming by friday EOD; 2) run bench in dev next week; 3) implement adaptive per-tenant batch caps; 4) add circuit-breaker presets to runbook; 5) share cost model for reserved/hybrid lanes
[33:26] Sofia: agreed, we'll sign off on soft throttle rule once you propose default threshold in runbook
[33:33] Daniel: timeline ok as long as bench is scheduled next week
[33:36] Jordan: nina will propose exact bench windows and run the first one with atlaspay traces
[33:41] Nina: yes targeting 2026-05-28 for initial bench, i'll send invite and pre-req checklist
[33:48] Marcus: I'll create the incident follow-up doc and share access to atlaspay team
[33:53] Priya: any concerns about rollbacks if throttles cause consumer impact? we need clear rollback steps
[33:59] Nina: runbook will include rollback: remove throttle rules, revert batch window, and re-enable default routing. we also include smoke checks to validate payment processing post-change
[34:12] Sofia: ok sounds good. thank you.
[34:15] Jordan: thanks everyone. final Qs?
[34:19] Daniel: none from me.
[34:21] Priya: all good here.
[34:24] Jordan: awesome. recap of action items and owners, i'll email the runbook now and follow up with invite for bench. Marcus will open the incident doc. Daniel to share scrubbed traces. we'll regroup 2026-06-01 for status
[34:41] Sofia: thanks all.
[34:44] Jordan: meeting adjourned.

References/links mentioned in-call:
- Runbook placeholder: https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/backpressure-atlaspay (will send final)
